result.title: Where the Image Sits: Vision-Text Order Bias in Jev
result.summary: Jev-style system-1 decision models read a choice from a single prefill. They restrict the next-token distribution to the supplied option labels and return a distribution over the options, with no generation and no parsing. Recent work shows that generative vision-language models are sensitive to the relative order of image and text tokens. We ask whether that sensitivity reaches this Jev-style readout. The answer is always read at the end of the prompt, so moving the image changes the distance from the visual evidence to the decision, but never the position at which the decision is read. Using four placements---prefix, pre-question, pre-options, and suffix---and holding the option listing fixed, we measure argmax flips, total variation, accuracy, calibration, and label marginals. Suffix placement flips 41.0% of decisions and lowers accuracy by 18.6 points. Averaged over the four slots, the curve is monotone, not U-shaped. That shape differs from prior results on generative vision-language models. The effect survives a battery of controls. We also introduce prefix--question averaging (P+Q), a two-forward readout that averages the prefix and pre-question distributions. It is at least as accurate as prefix and outperforms the prior baselines. Our code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/Youzhi333/Visual_Tex_Order_Bias_Jev.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文考察 Jev 式单次 prefill 决策模型中图文相对顺序的影响：在固定选项列表下比较 prefix、pre-question、pre-options、suffix 四种图像位置对 argmax 翻转率、总变差、准确率与校准的作用，并提出平均 prefix 与 pre-question 两个前向分布的 P+Q 读出。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于对视觉证据位置如何影响最终决策读出的诊断性失败分析，直接关联「答案是否真正使用视觉内容」与位置、注意力结构对内部视觉表示的效应；其无生成、单次读出的设定也便于核查证据到决策的通路，但结论是否可迁移到多步 latent 推理仍需阅读原文。
